ap_microeconomics-m01.stem: A museum charges a lower admission price to students than to other adults and checks identification at the door. Which statement best explains why the museum can increase its profit this way?

options.text: Students are more sensitive to price than other adults, and the identification check prevents resale of student tickets.
options.why: Separating more elastic and less elastic buyers and preventing resale lets the museum raise profit with different prices.

options.text: The identification check is irrelevant, because students could resell tickets to other adults.
options.why: The check prevents resale, which is a condition for the strategy to work.

options.text: Students cost more to serve than other adults, so they must pay a higher price.
options.why: Pricing in this way depends on elasticity of demand, not on a higher cost of serving a group.

options.text: The museum gains profit only if all visitors pay the same price, because separate prices confuse visitors.
options.why: Charging different prices to groups with different elasticities raises profit.

options.text: Students are less sensitive to price than other adults, so the discount raises the number of student visits.
options.why: A discount helps only where buyers are price sensitive, so students must be the more elastic group.

facts: variant=A museum charges a lower admission price

options.why: Charging more where demand is less elastic and less where it is more elastic raises profit if resale is prevented.

options.text: The two groups have the same elasticity, so different prices raise profit by confusing buyers.
options.why: With identical elasticities there is no gain from charging different prices.

options.text: Businesses can easily resell the program to schools, so the lower price protects the company.
options.why: Easy resale would undermine the price difference.

options.text: The company's marginal cost is lower for schools, so schools must pay a lower price.
options.why: Price discrimination is based on willingness to pay and elasticity, not on a difference in marginal cost.

options.text: Schools have less elastic demand than businesses, so a lower price raises revenue from schools.
options.why: A price cut raises revenue only where demand is elastic, which is the more price-sensitive group.

ap_microeconomics-m06.stem: A seasonal ice cream stand in a competitive market has fixed costs that it must pay all year whether or not it opens. In the winter, the price it can charge is below its average variable cost at every quantity. Which statement best describes what the stand should do in the winter?

options.text: Close for the winter, because opening would lose more than the fixed costs it must pay anyway.
options.why: When price is below average variable cost, opening adds losses beyond fixed cost, so temporary closure is better.

options.text: Stay open, because the price is below average total cost, so closing would end all costs.
options.why: Fixed costs continue even if the stand is closed in the short run.

options.text: Close permanently, because a short-run loss requires leaving the industry.
options.why: A short-run shutdown does not require leaving the market for good.

options.text: Raise the price, because a competitive firm can set any price it chooses.
options.why: A competitive firm is a price taker and cannot set its price.

options.text: Stay open, because the stand still earns some revenue to cover fixed costs.
options.why: Revenue below variable cost makes the loss larger than the fixed cost alone.
